questions.question: What absorbs the energy from light falling on a photovoltaic cell?

choices.A: Protons
choices.B: Photons
choices.C: Electrons
choices.D: Holes

questions.answer: Electrons

questions.question: What happens to photoconductive material when light shines on it?

choices.A: Resistance decreases
choices.B: Resistance increases
choices.C: Reflectivity increases
choices.D: Reflectivity decreases

questions.answer: Resistance decreases

questions.question: What is the most common configuration of an optoisolator or optocoupler?

choices.A: A lens and a photomultiplier
choices.B: A frequency-modulated helium-neon laser
choices.C: An amplitude-modulated helium-neon laser
choices.D: An LED and a phototransistor

questions.answer: An LED and a phototransistor

questions.question: What is the photovoltaic effect?

choices.A: The conversion of voltage to current when exposed to light
choices.B: The conversion of light to electrical energy
choices.C: The effect that causes a photodiode to emit light when a voltage is applied
choices.D: The effect that causes a phototransistor’s beta to decrease when exposed to light

questions.answer: The conversion of light to electrical energy

questions.question: Which of the following describes an optical shaft encoder?

choices.A: A device that detects rotation by interrupting a light source with a patterned wheel
choices.B: A device that measures the strength of a beam of light using analog-to-digital conversion
choices.C: An optical computing device in which light is coupled between devices by fiber optics
choices.D: A device for generating RTTY signals by means of a rotating light source

questions.answer: A device that detects rotation by interrupting a light source with a patterned wheel

questions.question: Which of these materials is most commonly used to create photoconductive devices?

choices.A: Polyphenol acetate
choices.B: Argon
choices.C: Crystalline semiconductor
choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.answer: Crystalline semiconductor

questions.question: What is a solid-state relay?

choices.A: A relay that uses transistors to drive the relay coil
choices.B: A device that uses semiconductors to implement the functions of an electromechanical relay
choices.C: A mechanical relay that latches in the on or off state each time it is pulsed
choices.D: A semiconductor switch that uses a monostable multivibrator circuit

questions.answer: A device that uses semiconductors to implement the functions of an electromechanical relay

questions.question: Why are optoisolators often used in conjunction with solid-state circuits that control 120 VAC circuits?

choices.A: Optoisolators provide a low-impedance link between a control circuit and a power circuit
choices.B: Optoisolators provide impedance matching between the control circuit and power circuit
choices.C: Optoisolators provide an electrical isolation between a control circuit and the circuit being switched
choices.D: Optoisolators eliminate the effects of reflected light in the control circuit

questions.answer: Optoisolators provide an electrical isolation between a control circuit and the circuit being switched

questions.question: What is the efficiency of a photovoltaic cell?

choices.A: The output RF power divided by the input DC power
choices.B: The output in lumens divided by the input power in watts
choices.C: The open-circuit voltage divided by the short-circuit current under full illumination
choices.D: The relative fraction of light that is converted to current

questions.answer: The relative fraction of light that is converted to current

questions.question: What is the most common material used in power-generating photovoltaic cells?

choices.A: Selenium
choices.B: Silicon
choices.C: Cadmium sulfide
choices.D: Indium arsenide

questions.answer: Silicon

questions.question: What is the approximate open-circuit voltage produced by a fully illuminated silicon photovoltaic cell?

choices.A: 0.5 volts
choices.B: 0.7 volts
choices.C: 1.1 volts
choices.D: 1.5 volts

questions.answer: 0.5 volts

questions.question: How does a linear electronic voltage regulator work?

choices.A: It has a ramp voltage as its output
choices.B: It eliminates the need for a pass transistor
choices.C: The control element duty cycle is proportional to the line or load conditions
choices.D: The conduction of a control element is varied to maintain a constant output voltage

questions.answer: The conduction of a control element is varied to maintain a constant output voltage

questions.question: How does a switchmode voltage regulator work?

choices.A: By alternating the output between positive and negative voltages
choices.B: By varying the duty cycle of pulses input to a filter
choices.C: By varying the conductivity of a pass element
choices.D: By switching between two Zener diode reference voltages

questions.answer: By varying the duty cycle of pulses input to a filter

questions.question: What device is used as a stable voltage reference?

choices.A: A Zener diode
choices.B: A digital-to-analog converter
choices.C: An SCR
choices.D: An analog-to-digital converter

questions.answer: A Zener diode

questions.question: Which of the following describes a three-terminal voltage regulator?

choices.A: A series current source
choices.B: A series regulator
choices.C: A shunt regulator
choices.D: A shunt current source

questions.answer: A series regulator

questions.question: Which of the following types of linear voltage regulator operates by loading the unregulated voltage source?

choices.A: A constant current source
choices.B: A series regulator
choices.C: A shunt current source
choices.D: A shunt regulator

questions.answer: A shunt regulator

questions.question: What is the purpose of Q1 in the circuit shown in Figure E7-2?

choices.A: It provides negative feedback to improve regulation
choices.B: It provides a constant load for the voltage source
choices.C: It controls the current to keep the output voltage constant
choices.D: It provides regulation by switching or “chopping” the input DC voltage

questions.answer: It controls the current to keep the output voltage constant

questions.question: What is the purpose of C2 in the circuit shown in Figure E7-2?

choices.A: It bypasses rectifier output ripple around D1
choices.B: It is a brute force filter for the output
choices.C: To prevent self-oscillation
choices.D: To provide fixed DC bias for Q1

questions.answer: It bypasses rectifier output ripple around D1

questions.question: What type of circuit is shown in Figure E7-2?

choices.A: Switching voltage regulator
choices.B: Common emitter amplifier
choices.C: Linear voltage regulator
choices.D: Common base amplifier

questions.question: How is battery operating time calculated?

choices.A: Average current divided by capacity in amp-hours
choices.B: Average current divided by internal resistance
choices.C: Capacity in amp-hours divided by average current
choices.D: Internal resistance divided by average current

questions.answer: Capacity in amp-hours divided by average current

questions.question: Why is a switching type power supply less expensive and lighter than an equivalent linear power supply?

choices.A: The inverter design does not require an output filter circuit
choices.B: The control circuitry uses less current, therefore smaller heat sinks are required
choices.C: The high frequency inverter design uses much smaller transformers and filter components for an equivalent power output
choices.D: It recovers power from the unused portion of the AC cycle, thus using fewer components

questions.answer: The high frequency inverter design uses much smaller transformers and filter components for an equivalent power output

questions.question: What is the purpose of an inverter connected to a solar panel output?

choices.A: Reduce AC ripple on the output
choices.B: Maintain voltage with varying illumination levels
choices.C: Prevent discharge when panel is not illuminated
choices.D: Convert the panel’s output from DC to AC

questions.answer: Convert the panel’s output from DC to AC

questions.question: What is the dropout voltage of a linear voltage regulator?

choices.A: Minimum input voltage for rated power dissipation
choices.B: Maximum output voltage drop when the input voltage is varied over its specified range
choices.C: Minimum input-to-output voltage required to maintain regulation
choices.D: Maximum that the output voltage may decrease at rated load

questions.answer: Minimum input-to-output voltage required to maintain regulation

questions.question: Which of the following calculates power dissipated by a series linear voltage regulator?

choices.A: Input voltage multiplied by input current
choices.B: Input voltage divided by output current
choices.C: Voltage difference from input to output multiplied by output current
choices.D: Output voltage multiplied by output current

questions.answer: Voltage difference from input to output multiplied by output current

questions.question: What is the purpose of connecting equal-value resistors across power supply filter capacitors connected in series?

choices.A: Equalize the voltage across each capacitor
choices.B: Discharge the capacitors when voltage is removed
choices.C: Provide a minimum load on the supply
choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.answer: All these choices are correct

questions.question: What is the purpose of a step-start circuit in a high-voltage power supply?

choices.A: To provide a dual-voltage output for reduced power applications
choices.B: To compensate for variations of the incoming line voltage
choices.C: To prevent arcing across the input power switch or relay contacts
choices.D: To allow the filter capacitors to charge gradually

questions.answer: To allow the filter capacitors to charge gradually
